claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a typical ferritic matrix.
As-received Q235 steel carries a naturally formed, ultrathin, heterogeneous surface oxide from ambient storage.
The native oxide on Q235 steel is primarily Fe3O4-rich.
The corrosion performance of pre-exposed Q235 steel is governed by the integrity of its native iron-oxide scale.
A continuous and intact native oxide scale can provide effective corrosion protection to Q235 steel.
A discontinuous or defective native oxide scale permits rapid degradation of Q235 steel.
Controlled annealing densifies and makes the native oxide film more uniform and adherent.
Annealing can cause grain growth or coarsening.
Annealing drives separate oxide patches to coalesce into a dense and uniform film on Q235 steel.
A dense and uniform iron-oxide film slows oxygen, ionic species, and salt penetration.
Nonuniform oxide coverage can create micro-galvanic cells that accelerate localized corrosion.
Annealed Q235 steel will have a lower corrosion rate than as-received Q235 steel in room-temperature chloride solution.
Annealed Q235 steel will have a lower corrosion rate than as-received Q235 steel in molten salt at 700–900 °C.
Relative to annealed specimens, untreated Q235 steel will exhibit more pitting, spallation, and severe corrosion morphology.
Untreated Q235 steel will degrade especially rapidly at high temperature because of oxidation and oxide-scale breakdown.
The proposed oxide-uniformity mechanism applies to low-alloy carbon steels such as Q235.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to stainless and highly alloyed steels because Cr, Ni, or other alloying elements produce distinct, more robust, self-healing passive films.
Salt chemistries that chemically alter the oxide can invalidate the proposed protection mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts improvement in both regimes, so failure in either regime would refute that universal prediction. The stated falsification rule instead requires no improvement in both regimes, leaving a mixed result incorrectly non-falsifying.
